# segment index

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:segmentIndex`](gmeow-segmentIndex.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/segmentIndex>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/documents`](../../slices/documents.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The position of this segment within its containing whole — 1-based by convention, but not enforced.

## Structure

**Property shape:** datatype property; [`gmeow:ContentSegment`](../classes/gmeow-ContentSegment.md) -> [`xsd:integer`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer); functional

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:segmentIndex`](gmeow-segmentIndex.md) from [`gmeow:ContentSegment`](../classes/gmeow-ContentSegment.md) to [`xsd:integer`](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Common Companion Terms

[`gmeow:ContentSegment`](../classes/gmeow-ContentSegment.md)

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to record the structural position of a content segment within its containing whole — the chapter or scene number; functional, 1-based by convention.

### Avoid when

- Avoid it for a subjective reading order (that is a [`gmeow:ReadingOrder`](../classes/gmeow-ReadingOrder.md) standpoint) and avoid relying on it across whole boundaries — the index is local to one container.

### How to use

- Carry the position integer on [`gmeow:segmentIndex`](gmeow-segmentIndex.md) alongside [`gmeow:segmentOf`](gmeow-segmentOf.md); perspectival orderings that differ from this structural index ride a [`gmeow:ReadingOrder`](../classes/gmeow-ReadingOrder.md).
